facility: Winchester Water Treatment Plant, Roseburg, Oregon
source: City of Roseburg, Water Treatment Facilities Preliminary Design Report, July 2009 (public record)
question: Can the Winchester Water Treatment Plant be expanded from its current 12 mgd to 18 mgd? For each unit along the flow path, determine whether it limits 18 mgd, the flow at which it becomes limiting, and the least-cost modification that makes 18 mgd work.

criteria.name: Current rated plant capacity
criteria.value: 12 mgd - treatment capacity limitation determined by the four existing filters

criteria.name: Planned expansion nominal capacity
criteria.value: 18 mgd - treatment capacity limitation based on ultimate buildout of six filters using same media as existing four

criteria.name: Hydraulic vs treatment capacity distinction
criteria.value: Hydraulic capacity is piping, pumping, volume and flow control limits; treatment capacity is ability to meet regulatory or industry standards

criteria.name: Hydraulic profile design basis
criteria.value: Developed during original design for maximum instantaneous flow of 18 mgd; updated based on field tests for maximum flow of 22 mgd

criteria.name: Firm pumping capacity definition
criteria.value: Maximum flow achievable with one of the largest installed pumps out of service

criteria.name: Maximum desirable pipeline velocity
criteria.value: Typically 6.0 fps in transmission main of this type; short segment of finished main allows higher as acceptable

criteria.name: Fish protection approach velocity
criteria.value: Maximum approach velocity 0.4 fps applies at 4-ft square gated openings outside fish screens, gates fully submerged

criteria.name: Clearwell storage guideline
criteria.value: Generally desirable minimum ~60 minutes detention at peak flow rate

criteria.name: Surge protection performance criteria
criteria.value: Protection to 9700 gpm (14.0 mgd); max upsurge 150 psi; min downsurge at HS station HGL 630 ft (~175 ft head or 75 psi assuming ground 455 ft)

criteria.name: Filter treatment rating basis
criteria.value: 3 mgd per filter treatment (12 mgd /4 filters; 18 mgd /6 filters same media); hydraulically 4 mgd per filter filtering to clearwell

criteria.name: Water rights availability
criteria.value: City has 20 mgd on North Umpqua River, exceeds 18 mgd; additional rights investigated

definitions.definition: Maximum flow with largest unit out of service, per water industry planning/operating conventions

collection.question: Can the Winchester WTP be expanded from 12 mgd to 18 mgd? For each unit along the flow path, does it limit 18 mgd, at what flow does it become limiting, and what least-cost modification makes 18 mgd work?

rfi.issue: Intake fish-screen hydraulic limit withheld: p.109 states 0.4 fps at 4-ft square gates fully submerged then [withheld] capacity conclusion
rfi.reason: Cannot quote limiting flow; need flow at which 0.4 fps is exceeded to judge 18 mgd
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Treat intake openings/screens as adequate to at least 18 mgd for this stage because p.109 states screens pass up to 18 mgd or more and river openings adequate to 24 mgd or more; fish-velocity calculation deferred to hydraulics runs (future labels INT-18, INT-24) - reason: use document's adequacy statements as governing until withheld clause recovered

rfi.issue: Conflicting raw-water firm capacity: nominal 16 mgd (p.108) vs 15.0 mgd in 2002 vs 14 mgd with Pumps 1,2,4 in 2006; Pump 3 noted substantially below rated but 2006 test without Pump 3 even lower
rfi.item: Raw water firm capacity at 18 mgd
rfi.reason: Unclear whether pumps degraded, system head increased, or test conditions differ; determines if 18 mgd needs pump replacement vs VFD/control only
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Adopt tested firm 14-15 mgd as governing existing condition, not nominal 16 mgd - reason: field tests (p.109) are more reliable than nameplate; any 18 mgd option must add/replace firm pumping and address TDH from 30-in main headloss

rfi.issue: High-service firm capacity statement truncated: p.115 gives nominally 10 mgd firm then notes three largest operate at ~3300 gpm each under current conditions then [withheld]
rfi.item: High-service firm and max with all pumps
rfi.reason: Cannot determine tested firm/max vs nominal 16/14 mgd on p.107; determines number of additional pumps for 18 mgd
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Adopt nominal firm 10 mgd as existing limit requiring added pumps for 18 mgd, with actual ~3300 gpm each noted but withheld total not assumed - reason: conservative use of only quoted nominal value until truncated clause recovered

rfi.issue: Typo/conflict p.116: paragraph on finished water main says velocities through the 30-inch raw water pipeline exceed 6.0 fps at ~18 mgd, but Table 4-3 (p.117) is finished water main
rfi.item: Which pipeline exceeds 6 fps at 18 mgd
rfi.reason: Affects whether raw, finished, or both exceed desirable velocity at 18 mgd
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Treat as drafting error and apply 6-fps exceedance at ~18 mgd to both 30-in raw (Table 4-1 5.9 fps at 18 mgd, p.110) and 30-in finished onsite (Table 4-3 5.97 fps at 18 mgd, p.117) - reason: both tables show ~6 fps at 18 mgd, and document states higher velocity acceptable for short onsite finished segment (p.116)

rfi.issue: Treatment capacity evaluation, CT analysis (Sec 3), Fig 4-1/4-2 hydraulic profile, and Sec 6 intake options not in available pages 107-119; filter 3-mgd basis, disinfection contact, floc/sed performance at cold/high-turbidity flows not quantified
rfi.item: Treatment limits at 18 mgd (filters, CT, pretreatment)
rfi.reason: Cannot judge treatment vs hydraulic limit for 18 mgd without criteria and contact-time calculations
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Treat 3 mgd/filter and second basin + two filters as treatment-required for 18 mgd per p.107/p.111, and treat clearwell CT/storage (57 min at 18 mgd, p.115) as check only - reason: document explicitly defines 12 and 18 mgd as treatment limits on that filter basis

rfi.issue: Offsite transmission WTP-to-Reservoir Hill future 30-in mains status unknown: p.118 anticipates new 30-in to replace 27-in plus second parallel 30-in in future, but whether built and hydraulic capacity at 18-24 mgd not in pages
rfi.reason: HS pumps + onsite main may pass 18 mgd while offsite system controls
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Exclude offsite transmission adequacy from 18 mgd plant-expansion verdict pending data; evaluate only onsite header/short 30-in main and surge to 14 mgd limit (p.117) - reason: available pages provide only onsite velocities/headloss and surge limit to 14 mgd

rfi.issue: Surge protection limited to 14 mgd (p.117) vs 18 mgd target; addition of second tank likely not practical due to space noted but full recommendation withheld
rfi.reason: Determines whether 18 mgd needs operating constraint vs new surge facility
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Flag surge as limiting above 14 mgd requiring re-analysis for 18 mgd - reason: quoted criteria explicitly caps existing protection at 14 mgd

rfi.issue: Wastewater/solids handling pages truncated mid-sentence after decant structure (p.119); basin equalization, dry beds, and ability to handle 18 mgd backwash/sludge volumes not quantified
rfi.item: Wastewater and solids limit at 18 mgd
rfi.reason: Cannot compute backwash equalization at 6-filter/18 mgd operation
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Treat WW pump firm 3000 gpm (p.119) and 2x300k-gal basins (p.119) as adequate for reporting but flag solids handling as TBD for 18 mgd - reason: avoid silent invention where text is cut off

standards.name: Firm capacity convention
standards.use: Use tested firm (largest unit out) as governing, not nameplate, for intake, HS, WW stations

standards.name: 6.0 fps desirable max in transmission mains
standards.use: Flag exceedance at ~18 mgd (RW and FW onsite) but allow higher if document states acceptable for short segment

standards.name: 60-min clearwell detention guideline
standards.use: Check 57 min at 18 mgd with six filters as approximately meeting minimum per p.115

standards.name: 0.4 fps fish approach velocity
standards.use: Apply at outside intake gates; use future hydraulics runs INT-18/INT-24 to compute, not hand calc
